name: @pipeworx/mcp-usaspending

tools.name: usa_spending_by_agency
tools.description: Break down US federal contract spending by agency for a given fiscal year (default: current year) and optional quarter (1-4). Returns agency names, abbreviations, and dollar amounts from USAspending.gov.

fiscal_year.description: Four-digit fiscal year (e.g., "2025"). Defaults to current year.

quarter.description: Fiscal quarter (1-4). Omit for full year.

tools.name: usa_award_search
tools.description: Search US federal PROCUREMENT CONTRACTS / government contract awards for goods and services. Use recipient_name for "contracts won by Lockheed Martin"; keywords searches award descriptions/topics, not contractor identity. Dates are optional and default to the last 12 months for "recent" questions. Dates select awards ACTIVE in the window (not signed in it) and award_amount is the award's LIFETIME obligation, so do not sum it as spending for the period. Results are paged: 100 per page max — pass `page` (and read `page_metadata.has_next`) to reach the rest. Returns recipient, award amount, outlays (with an outlays_reported flag, since DoD awards usually report none), dates, and contract type. Umbrella contracts (IDVs — CRS-2, NASA Launch Services II, CCtCap) are a SEPARATE result set in `idvs`, not in `awards`: read both, and `idv_status` says which you got. IDV and child-order amounts are disjoint, so `totals.combined_amount` is the correct total.

recipient_name.description: Contractor/recipient name (e.g., "Lockheed Martin"). Use for awards won by a company; do not put company names in keywords. Matched as a SUBSTRING of the registered legal name, so a brand name can miss the company entirely ("SpaceX" is not inside "SPACE EXPLORATION TECHNOLOGIES CORP."); a known brand that matches nothing is retried under its legal name and the response says so in `recipient_resolution`. An empty result distinguishes `no_match` (no registered recipient has this name) from `recipient_matched_no_awards` (it does, but holds nothing under your window/agency filters) and lists the near-miss names in `recipient_candidates`.

state.description: Place-of-performance US state, 2-letter code (e.g., "MD", "TX"). Filters to contracts performed in that state.

agency.description: Awarding agency — full toptier name ("Department of Defense") or the common abbreviation (DOD, DHS, VA, HHS, DOE, NASA, GSA, USDA, EPA…), which is expanded for you.

set_aside.description: Small-business set-aside filter. Accepts a family name ("HUBZone", "8(a)", "WOSB", "EDWOSB", "SDVOSB", "Veteran", "Small business", "Indian"), a FAR code ("HZC", "8AN", "SDVOSBC"), or the literal USAspending description ("HUBZONE SET-ASIDE"). Matches both the set-aside and sole-source variants of a family.

limit.description: Number of results per page (1-100, default 10)

page.description: 1-based page number (default 1). total_results can exceed limit; page through with this and read page_metadata.has_next / total_pages to reach every row. The `idvs` array is served on page 1 only.

include_idvs.description: Include umbrella contracts (indefinite delivery vehicles) as a separate `idvs` array. Default true. Leave it on: these are often a recipient's largest awards, and excluding them understates a total silently.

tools.name: usa_spending_by_category
tools.description: Analyze federal spending by industry, product/service, recipient, or agency. Returns spending totals per category. Use for market research and identifying government contracting opportunities.

category.description: Category to group by: naics, psc, recipient, awarding_agency, awarding_subagency

tools.name: usa_recipient_profile
tools.description: Answer "what federal contracts did [company] win recently?" and get a contractor's federal contract awards. Dates are optional and default to the last 12 months; the response always states the window used.

recipient_name.description: Recipient/contractor name to search for (e.g., "Lockheed Martin"). Matched as a substring of the registered legal name; a known brand name that matches nothing is retried under its legal name (`recipient_resolution` says so, and `recipient_name_searched` is what was actually queried).

tools.name: usa_spending_trends
tools.description: "How has [agency] contract spending trended over the last N fiscal years?" / "is [agency] spending on X growing?" / "federal spending history for [topic]" — US FEDERAL contract/award spending over time from USAspending.gov, grouped by fiscal year, quarter, or month. Filter by keywords or by federal agency (DHS/Homeland Security, DOD/Defense, HHS, VA, DOE, NASA, State, Treasury). Returns the historical dollar amount per period for trend and budget-forecasting questions. Federal only — for state & county award data use gov_contracts_search.

keywords.description: Keywords to track spending for (e.g., ["artificial intelligence"])

agency.description: Awarding agency name. Use instead of, or alongside, keywords.

start_date.description: Start date YYYY-MM-DD. Optional — defaults to five years ago; the window actually used comes back under `period`.

end_date.description: End date YYYY-MM-DD. Optional — defaults to today.

group.description: Time grouping: fiscal_year, quarter, or month (default fiscal_year)

tools.name: usa_expiring_awards
tools.description: Federal contracts EXPIRING soon -- the recompete calendar. "Which VA IT contracts over $10M expire in the next 12 months?" / "what is up for recompete at DHS next year" / "find follow-on opportunities in NAICS 5415" / "whose contract is ending". Returns the incumbent holding each award, its period of performance, obligated dollars, agency, NAICS/PSC, and a usaspending.gov link. Filter by agency, sub-agency, NAICS or PSC prefix, incumbent name, and minimum obligated dollars. Covers awarded CONTRACTS already held by a vendor; for open solicitations still accepting bids use samgov/govcon tools.

agency.description: Awarding agency, substring match (e.g. "Department of Veterans Affairs", "Defense").

sub_agency.description: Awarding sub-agency, substring match (e.g. "Veterans Health Administration").

naics.description: NAICS code or prefix. Hierarchical: "5415" matches all 6-digit computer-services codes beneath it.

psc.description: Product/Service Code or prefix (e.g. "D3" for IT services).

min_amount.description: Minimum total OBLIGATED dollars on the award (not the ceiling). 10000000 for "over $10M".

months_ahead.description: Window size in months from today (default 12).

tools.name: usa_incumbent_profile
tools.description: Federal contract portfolio for one contractor -- "what does Leidos hold and when does it expire", "which of Booz Allen's contracts come up for recompete", incumbent research before a bid. Returns active award count, total obligated, ceiling, expirations at 6/12/18 months, top agencies and NAICS, and the next awards to expire with dates.

limit.description: How many upcoming expirations to list (default 10, max 100).

instructions: @pipeworx/mcp-usaspending forwards to the Pipeworx gateway and lists only the usaspending pack's tools. Set PIPEWORX_META_TOOLS=1 to also list ask_pipeworx and the other gateway-wide tools.
